svg.title: History, capabilities, directions, and representative methods of agent self-evolution
svg.desc: A dense overview of six historical phases, capability growth, ten research directions, paradigm shifts, and twenty-three published milestone methods with concise method descriptions.
svg.text: Agent Self-Evolution: History, Capability Growth, Directions, and Representative Methods
From foundation-model precursors to persistent memory, skill ecosystems, workflow search, multimodal adaptation, and governed release
A · Six historical phases: the update target expands from model parameters to the whole agent system

g.text: Reason, act, observe, reflect, and reuse
Optimize memory, skills, prompts, and graphs

svg.text: C · Ten directions formed from four big questions

g.text: D1 admission & scope · D6 negative-evolution evaluation
D2 memory · D3 skills/tools · D4 routing/contracts
Q3 · What is changing around the agent?
D5 embodiment/world · D9 goals/users · D10 collective evolution
Q4 · How can evolution stay controlled?
Should this lesson be stored, and where is it valid?
How should accepted experience be maintained?
How does experience become executable capability?
Which component changes, and will updates compose?
World adaptation · evaluation · security · governance · goals · collective evolution
Directions are lifecycle questions, not competing algorithms. A paper idea chooses one identifiable variable inside one direction.
Autonomous proposal → governed release: audit, safety, provenance, rollback, and resource control become part of the method rather than afterthoughts.

svg.text: E · Published milestones grouped by method family — each card states what the method actually does

g.text: Generate rationales, filter by answers, and retrain
Bootstrap instruction data from the model itself
LLM iteratively proposes better prompts or solutions
Write verbal feedback into episodic memory
Learn retrospective feedback to optimize policy
Update: feedback policy · Signal: trajectory return
Reuse navigation history and imagined futures
Update: navigation memory · Signal: trajectory history
Experience methods convert outcomes or trajectories
into reusable state that changes later behavior.
Self-supervised learning of when to call tools
Update: tool-use policy · Signal: tool utility
Explore and grow an executable skill library
Close the loop between visual tool use and update
Create/select visual APIs from execution feedback
Search executable agent programs and scaffolds
Use MCTS to construct and optimize workflows
Update: workflow graph · Signal: execution score
Online curriculum RL from web interaction
Update: policy parameters · Signal: web reward
System methods search over prompts, graphs,
modules, or policies, then retain candidates that
perform well under an evaluator or environment.
Train an independent VLM critic to catch errors
Update: memory graph · Signal: retrieval feedback
Visual correction is not yet equivalent to safe,
